title: Levelwise isomorphisms and complete cones
statement:
Fix the adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] on $T_{\Proet}$, with $A_T=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $P_n=A/I^n$. All derived categories of coefficients below are categories of $A_T$-module sheaves, and every finite reduction means $K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, regarded as an $A_T$-module object by restriction of scalars. Derived completeness means that the Koszul completion map of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism.

A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after $\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T=0$ for every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Represent a derived tower morphism up to an isomorphism in the arrow category by the localization of a chain map. This is possible because the homotopy quotient is full and essentially surjective, and the derived homotopy localization is essentially surjective on arrows [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Exact evaluation commutes with localization [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. If all derived evaluations of the original map are invertible, the localized evaluated chain maps are invertible, so the evaluated chain maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Quasi-isomorphisms of complexes of towers are detected levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], as formalized by HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation. Hence the representing chain map is a quasi-isomorphism, its localization is invertible, and the original arrow is invertible. This directly implements joint conservativity without constructing cone triangles.

proof.text: For a complete object C, the unit-compatible intrinsic comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies the functorial Koszul unit followed by an isomorphism with the specified intrinsic unit [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Cancel that isomorphism to see that the functorial Koszul unit is invertible. Reconstruction then makes the canonical quotient completion unit C to Rlim(C_bullet) invertible. If all finite reductions vanish, evaluate the zero arrow 0 to C_bullet: its source and target are zero at each level by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], so all its evaluations are invertible. Step 1 makes this zero arrow invertible, hence C_bullet is zero. The ordinary inverse-limit functor is additive; its total right derived functor preserves zero objects (Functor.isZero_rightDerivedFunctor_obj). Therefore Rlim(C_bullet) is zero, and the invertible completion unit shows C is zero.

proof.text: For a map u between complete objects C and D, its reduction-tower map has invertible evaluations by the definition of finite reduction [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and is therefore invertible by step 1. Its image under reconstructionRlim is invertible. Step 3 makes both quotient completion units invertible. Naturality of the already stated reconstructionCompletionUnit of [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] gives u followed by comp_D equal to comp_C followed by Rlim(u_bullet). The latter composite is invertible; cancelling comp_D proves u invertible. No exactness or completeness-of-cones argument is required.

lean.statement: theorem completedAdic_levelwise_isomorphism_cones (T : Scheme.{t}) {A : Type t} [CommRing A] (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = d.ideal) : (∀ (M N : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicTowers T d)) (u : M ⟶ N), (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((completedAdicEvaluation T d n).map u)) → IsIso u ∧ ∀ (RF : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicTowers T d) ⥤ DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d)) (η : (lim : CompletedAdicTowers T d ⥤ CompletedAdicModules T d).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF), RF.IsRightDerivedFunctor η (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso (CompletedAdicTowers T d) (ComplexShape.up ℤ)) → IsIso (RF.map u)) ∧ (∀ C : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d), IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha C → (∀ n : ℕ, IsZero ((completedAdicFiniteReduction T d n).obj C)) → IsZero C) ∧ (∀ (C D : DerivedCategory (CompletedAdicModules T d)) (u : C ⟶ D), IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha C → IsCompletedAdicDerivedComplete T d r a ha D → (∀ n : ℕ, IsIso ((completedAdicFiniteReduction T d n).map u)) → IsIso u)

blueprint_update.statement:
A morphism in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_{A}(T))$ whose evaluation at every $n$ is
an isomorphism is itself an isomorphism and remains an isomorphism after
$\Rlim$. If a derived complete object $C$ satisfies $C\otimes_A^LP_n=0$ for
every $n$, then $C=0$. Consequently a morphism between derived complete
objects is an isomorphism once every finite reduction is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
The evaluation functors of [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] are jointly
conservative on the tower category, and $\Rlim$ is a triangulated functor ([prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality]), so
the first assertion holds. For a derived complete $C$,
[prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction] identifies $C$ with $\Rlim C_\bullet$,
and the vanishing of every finite reduction kills the tower $C_\bullet$
levelwise, hence $C=0$; the cone of a morphism between derived complete
objects is again derived complete, so the last assertion follows from the
second.
